# Start-ZbxPassiveAgent

## SYNOPSIS

Starts a passive agent as a session: a listener that answers the built-in keys to whichever server asks, until stopped.

## SYNTAX

```
Start-ZbxPassiveAgent [-Name] <string> [[-HostName] <string>] [[-AllowedPeer] <string[]>] [-Address <string>] [-Port <int>] [-CheckTimeout <TimeSpan>] [-TlsAccept <ZabbixTlsAcceptModes[]>] [-PassThru] [-KeyRule <string[]>] [-NoBundledItems] [-Plugin <string[]>] [-PluginPath <string>] [-PluginSetting <Hashtable>] [-PskIdentity <string>] [-Psk <SecureString>] [-Certificate <string>] [-CertificateKey <string>] [-CertificateAuthority <string>] [-CertificateRevocationList <string>] [-ServerIssuer <string>] [-ServerSubject <string>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Start-ZbxPassiveAgent cmdlet starts a passive agent as a session of this runspace: a listener on -Port (10050 by default) that answers the built-in keys (agent.ping, agent.version, agent.hostname, system.uname, and the bundled items: Zabbix's own system, process, file, network and web keys, such as vfs.fs.size and proc.num) and every handler registered on it, to the peers -AllowedPeer lets in. -KeyRule limits which keys it answers, with Zabbix's AllowKey and DenyKey lines, and -NoBundledItems leaves the bundled items out. -AllowedPeer is the agent's Server= line and defaults to 127.0.0.1 and ::1 only, as Zabbix's own agent does. Give the agent's credentials (-PskIdentity and -Psk, or -Certificate, -CertificateKey and -CertificateAuthority) to require TLS: the listener then accepts those kinds only, unless -TlsAccept says otherwise, and without credentials it accepts unencrypted connections only. Stop-ZbxPassiveAgent ends the session, and -PassThru writes it.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Start a passive agent and query it

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Port 30150
Get-ZbxAgentItem -Agent '127.0.0.1:30150' -Key 'agent.ping', 'agent.hostname' | Select-Object Key, Value
Stop-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

The session listens on -Port (10050 by default) in the background of this runspace and answers the built-in keys (agent.ping, agent.version, agent.hostname, system.uname, and Zabbix's own keys such as vfs.fs.size) to whoever -AllowedPeer lets in: loopback only by default.

### Example 2: Let the Zabbix server poll the agent

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -AllowedPeer '127.0.0.1', '10.0.0.0/24' -Address '127.0.0.1' `
    -Port 30150 -PassThru | Select-Object Name, Kind, Started
Stop-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

-AllowedPeer is Zabbix's Server= line: IP addresses, CIDR blocks or DNS names. Anything not listed is refused. -Address binds one interface instead of every one; -PassThru writes the session.

### Example 3: Answer only the keys you allow

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Port 30150 -KeyRule 'AllowKey=agent.*', 'AllowKey=vfs.fs.*[*]', 'DenyKey=*'
Get-ZbxAgentItem -Agent '127.0.0.1:30150' -Key 'vfs.fs.size[/,pfree]', 'proc.num' | Select-Object Key, Value, Error
Stop-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

-KeyRule takes Zabbix's AllowKey and DenyKey lines, tried in order: here the agent answers agent.* and vfs.fs.* keys and nothing else. A denied key is answered as "This agent does not answer the key.", as a key nobody answers is.

### Example 4: Answer a key of your own

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Port 30150
Register-ZbxPassiveAgentHandler -Name 'web-agent' -Key 'app.health' -ScriptBlock { 'ok' }
Get-ZbxAgentItem -Agent '127.0.0.1:30150' -Key 'app.health' | Select-Object Key, Value, IsSupported
Stop-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

A scriptblock registered on the session answers its key; the server (or Get-ZbxAgentItem) sees an ordinary item.

### Example 5: Keep an agent running for the length of a script

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Port 30150
try {
    (Get-ZbxAgentItem -Agent '127.0.0.1:30150' -Key 'agent.version').Value
}
finally {
    Stop-ZbxPassiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
}
```

A script that serves checks while it does its own work, and always stops the listener, even on failure.

### -KeyRule

Which keys the agent answers, as lines of Zabbix's agent configuration, tried in order, the first that matches deciding: 'AllowKey=vfs.file.*[*]', 'DenyKey=*'. In a pattern * matches any characters, in the name or in a parameter. Without it the agent answers every key but system.run, as Zabbix's agents do. A denied key is answered as one nobody answers.

### -Plugin

Plugins to load into the agent, by name: each a folder under -PluginPath holding a plugin's dotnet publish output, whose item keys the agent then answers beside the built-in keys and the session's scriptblock handlers. A plugin that cannot be loaded fails the start, and a plugin whose files other accounts can write is refused on Linux and macOS.
